lines.say: In December 2001, its banks were running out of dollars. So the government did something drastic: it froze people's savings.
You could take out 250 pesos a week, nothing more. Argentines called it the corralito, the little corral.
The anger poured into the streets. People banged pots and pans outside their windows, then marched.
The president answered with a state of siege.
It only made things worse. Riots tore through the Plaza de Mayo, and across the country, thirty-nine people were killed.
That evening, Fernando de la Rúa resigned, and left the presidential palace by helicopter.
His successor announced the largest debt default the world had ever seen. He was gone within a week.
In under two weeks, Argentina went through five presidents.
